Class WindowSignals

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.WindowSignals
public final class WindowSignals extends Object
The client-observed slot INTERACTION signals — which slot the cursor is over (hovered) and which slot was last clicked (selected), as Addresses. The interaction sibling of ObservedReactions (which observes content): both are pure client observers keyed by address through ClientSlotAddressing.

Address-keyed, by design

A consumer reacts to its OWN addressed things — WindowSignals.isHovered(addr) / isSelected(addr) where addr is a panel/created-slot address it minted by id. It does NOT ask "what vanilla index is hovered" — addressing by identity is what makes a rule work the same in creative and survival (a created slot has one address in both). The hover/click are captured by MKClient (hover each client tick; selection on a screen click; cleared on close) and mapped through the shared addressing, so a hovered created slot reports its created address.

Client-thread only.

    • tickHover

      @Internal public static void tickHover(@Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.AbstractContainerMenu menu, @Nullable net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot hoveredSlot)
      Update the hovered slot (MKClient, each client tick). Null clears it.

      Internal write feeder. Only MK's client tick feeds the signals; it takes raw vanilla Slots straight off the live screen. Consumers READ the signals through the public address-keyed/display API below (isHovered(Address)/hoveredName/…); they never feed them.

    • clearSelection

      @Internal public static void clearSelection()
      Clear the selection (MKClient, when a container screen closes).

      Internal write feeder (see tickHover(AbstractContainerMenu, Slot)/recordClick(AbstractContainerMenu, Slot)) — the third member of the write trio. Only MK's client lifecycle calls it; consumers read the selection through the public API (isSelected(Address)/selectedName) and never reset it themselves.
